slides.title: Leading Without a Direct Reporting Line
bullets: One of the most determining and hardest competencies to develop in Medical Affairs
The function rarely holds hierarchical authority over the teams it must coordinate with
Commercial, market access and clinical research all require constant cross-functional coordination

slides.title: Credibility Comes Before Influence
bullets: Nobody sustainably follows someone they don't see as genuinely competent
Scientific rigor and reliable information are the base of all influence
Consistency between what you say and what you do matters just as much

slides.eyebrow: Build It Before You Need It
slides.title: Networks and Evidence-Based Persuasion
bullets: Cultivate trust with key stakeholders before you need their collaboration
A prior relationship makes the ask-for-support conversation far more receptive
Connect your goal explicitly to the other party's own interests and priorities
This earns genuine support, not superficial compliance

slides.title: Listen First, Then Adapt the Message
bullets: Understand each function's concerns and language before presenting anything
A market access lead, a medical director and a clinical investigator care about different things
Adapt how an idea is framed without compromising its scientific content or independence

slides.title: Persuasion Over Positional Authority
bullets: Minimize any display of authority and lead through reasoned persuasion instead
Leaders who avoid imposing their position earn more solid, lasting support
This beats relying on formal hierarchy to get buy-in

slides.title: The Voice That Gets Sought Out
bullets: Medical Affairs has no direct commercial decision power but indispensable scientific knowledge
Mastering influence without authority is what gets that voice heard and integrated
Over time, it becomes the voice proactively sought in major strategic decisions

takeaway.title: Influence without authority turns scientific credibility into real strategic weight
bullets: Credibility built on rigor and consistency is the non-negotiable starting point
Networks, evidence-based persuasion and message adaptation build influence deliberately
Leading through persuasion, not positional authority, earns more lasting support
